analyst_view.overall: Early view: Brann (7th, seven points) are unbeaten in Europe after beating Lincoln and Kauno Zalgiris and drawing 1-1 at Sint-Truiden, though they are only seventh in a very open Eliteserien season (45 goals for, 42 against in 25 games). AGF (24th, two points) are eighth in Denmark with six draws in 13 games and have scored once in three European games. Brann are favourites at home.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean lower: AGF's European games ended 1-0, 1-1 and 0-0, and their Danish league record (17 goals for, 21 against in 13) is low-scoring. Brann's games are much more open, but AGF set the tempo in Europe so far.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.0 corners, 7.6 for Brann. Brann at home should have a lot of the ball against a side that has kept things tight, which fits the high home split; I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Neither side has a disciplinary pattern I could find in this competition and no referee is known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 18.5 for Brann. Brann's open style supports a high home count, while AGF's caution keeps theirs down. That matches the split, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: AGF have scored one goal in three European games, so their 3.7 looks generous, and a deep AGF block should cut down Brann's clean shooting chances.
